title: Final twisted-arrow resolution of a cartesian fibration with terminal fibres
statement:
Use quasicategories, ordinary nerves, coherent functors, transformations and mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and cartesian fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $A$ be a small ordinary category and let $p:R\to N(A)^{\mathrm{op}}$ be a cartesian fibration of quasicategories in a containing universe. Suppose that each fibre $R_a$ has a terminal object $t_a$, meaning that $\operatorname{Map}_{R_a}(r,t_a)$ is contractible for every $r\in R_a$. No transport-preservation assumption on these terminal objects is made. For $u:a\to b$ in $A$, write $u^*:R_a\to R_b$ for cartesian transport along $u^{\mathrm{op}}:b\to a$ in $N(A)^{\mathrm{op}}$.

Define $K_A=N(\operatorname{Tw}(A)^{\mathrm{op}})$ as follows: its objects are arrows $u:a\to b$ of $A$, and an arrow $u\to u'$ is a pair $f:a\to a'$, $g:b'\to b$ with $u=gu'f$. There is a coherent functor $k:K_A\to R$ over the projection $u:a\to b\mapsto b$ to $N(A)^{\mathrm{op}}$, with $k(u)\simeq u^*t_a$. On the arrow $(f,g)$ its component is the composite
$$u^*t_a\simeq g^*u'^*f^*t_a\longrightarrow g^*u'^*t_{a'}\longrightarrow u'^*t_{a'},$$
where the middle map is induced by the map to the terminal object $t_{a'}$ and the last arrow is cartesian over $g^{\mathrm{op}}$. The compatible terminal-object and cartesian-lift choices can be made coherently, and any two such constructions are naturally equivalent over $N(A)^{\mathrm{op}}$.

This functor $k$ is final in the following strong sense. For every quasicategory $D$ in any further containing universe, coherent diagram $V:R\to D$ and $d\in D$, restriction itself induces an equivalence of spaces
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(R,D)}(V,\Delta_Rd)\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ \operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K_A,D)}(Vk,\Delta_{K_A}d),$$
natural in $V,d$. Consequently a specified cocone on $V$ is colimiting if and only if its restriction along $k$ is colimiting; existence of either colimit implies existence of the other with that cocone. The total $R$ and its mapping spaces need not be small in the universe in which $A$ is small.

source.place: Agent terminal-fibre generalization of the twisted-diagonal contraction in Section 5.6, Proposition 5.6.9, pp. 241-242. The statement here is for a given cartesian fibration, not a classification theorem; see report.md for the comma contraction and the distinction from the source assertion. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical lemma.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-terminal-comparison-coherence] to the pullback of $p$ over every simplex of $N(A)^{\mathrm{op}}$, with diagonal objects $t_a$. Its boundary restriction is a trivial Kan fibration. Induct over nondegenerate simplices of $N(A)$: prescribed proper faces are a diagram on $B_n$, so choose an extension in $\mathcal L(N(T_n))$; assign degeneracies by restriction. The posets $T_n$ cover the twisted index: every chain of nested intervals is contained in a composable chain of $A$. These local diagrams therefore assemble to $k$. A fixed-source edge is cartesian, and factoring a square $(f,g)$ through its fixed-target and fixed-source parts gives precisely the displayed terminal-comparison/cartesian edge formula. For two constructions, extend the two endpoints over a parameter interval and then its higher boundaries using the same relative lifting assertion. Vertex components are equivalences since the local choice spaces are contractible Kan complexes. The componentwise criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] makes the comparison a natural equivalence over the base. No transport-terminality assumption enters.

source.place: Agent construction from terminal comparisons and cartesian lifts; the twisted-diagonal comparison of Proposition 5.6.9 is motivation, not an assertion of this generalization.

proof.text: Fix $r\in R_c$. Define $C_r=K_A\times_R R_{r/}$ with the join coslice, whose $n$-simplices are the maps $\Delta^0\star\Delta^n\to R$ starting at $r$. Its target projection is a left fibration by the opposite of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration]; its pullback to $K_A$ is consequently a quasicategory. A comma object has the form $(u:a\to b,\beta:r\to k(u))$, and $p\beta=w^{\mathrm{op}}$ for a unique $w:b\to c$, since the base is an ordinary nerve. The source-fixed edges of $k$ are cartesian by step 1. Apply [lem-coef-cartesian-comma-normalization] to obtain $H$ and its transformation to the identity, with $H(u,w,\beta)=(wu,h)$ and the full cartesian factorization triangle. On comma arrows the base triangle reads $w'=wg$ and $wu=w'u'f$, so the induced twisted pair of $H$ is $(f,1_c)$. This invokes the lemma's simplexwise assertion, rather than assuming that objectwise factorization is functorial.

source.place: Agent comma calculation for the terminal-fibre generalization of Section 5.6; factorization of the base edge and its parameter simplices.

proof.text:
There is a coherent transformation $H\to\mathrm{id}_{C_r}$. At $(u,w,\beta)$ it is the twisted arrow $(1_a,w):wu\to u$, with its cartesian factorization triangle $\beta\simeq (\mathrm{cart}_w)h$. Choose a terminal cone in $R_c$ by [lem-coef-infinity-normalized-final-cone]. Write $\rho:r\to t_c$ for its component at $r$, and put $z=(1_c:c\to c,\rho)$ in $C_r$. There is a second coherent transformation $H\to\Delta z$: its twisted pair is $(wu,1_c):wu\to1_c$, and its triangle compares $r\xrightarrow h(wu)^*t_a\to t_c$ with $\rho$. The comparison to $t_c$ here is the one used to construct $k$ in step 1. The terminal-boundary extension theorem gives these triangles and all their parameter coherences relative to that chosen comparison; no equality of two arbitrarily chosen maps to $t_c$ is asserted. On an arrow of $C_r$ the required equality of twisted pairs is $(w'u')f=wu$, already established in step 2. Thus the two transformations give a zigzag
$$\mathrm{id}_{C_r}\ \longleftarrow\ H\ \longrightarrow\ \Delta z.$$
On realizations they are homotopies: triangulate each prism $|\Delta^n|\times[0,1]$ by its monotone lattice paths and evaluate the transformation on the corresponding simplices of $\Delta^n\times\Delta^1$. The face restrictions agree, so these maps descend through the realization quotient. Concatenating the first one backwards with the second contracts the identity to the constant map at $z$. Consequently $C_r$ is weakly contractible. This is a contraction of the whole coherent comma category, including all higher simplices, rather than only of its homotopy category.

source.place: Agent explicit twisted-comma contraction: replace the arrow u by wu and then map wu to the identity of c.

proof.text:
To obtain restriction on cocone spaces without a circular appeal to an existing cofinality theorem, enlarge to a universe in which $R$ is small and factor $k$ by the small-object theorem [lem-coef-small-object-cell-factorization], using the set of right horns $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, $0<i\leq n$. In simplicial sets colimits are computed degreewise. Each horn is generated by finitely many nondegenerate simplices, so its maps into an increasing countable sequence of horn-cell inclusions factor at a finite stage; equality of two such maps is also detected at a finite stage. Thus the smallness hypothesis holds with $\kappa=\aleph_0$. The theorem gives
$$K_A\xrightarrow{j}E\xrightarrow{q}R,\qquad qj=k,$$
where $j$ is a right-horn cell map and $q$ lifts all right horns. In the terminology of [def-coef-infinity-right-anodyne] and [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], $j$ is right anodyne and $q$ is a right fibration. Since $R$ is a quasicategory, filling an inner horn first in $R$ and then along $q$ proves that $E$ is a quasicategory. All sets of attaching squares are small in the chosen enlarged universe.

source.place: Agent use of the one-sided horn small-object factorization; compare the factorization characterization before Proposition 4.4.4.

proof.text:
Let $S_r=R_{r/}$ be the join coslice. By the opposite of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration], its target projection $S_r\to R$ is a left fibration. By the explicit simplex definition in step 2, $K_A\times_R S_r=C_r$ as simplicial sets; no comparison between distinct comma models is required. Put $D_r=E\times_R S_r$. The pullback of $j$ along the left fibration $D_r\to E$ is
$$K_A\times_R S_r\longrightarrow D_r.$$
It is right anodyne by [lem-coef-left-fibration-right-anodyne-base-change]. The Kan-Quillen theorem [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] makes every horn inclusion a trivial cofibration and closes these under cell attachments and retracts. Hence this pullback is a weak homotopy equivalence. Step 3 implies that $D_r$ is weakly contractible.

source.place: Proposition 4.4.11 with Proposition 4.4.4(iv), plus the agent right-anodyne comparison of comma models.

proof.text: The identity is initial in $S_r=R_{r/}$ by the opposite of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-equivalence-final]. The opposite of [lem-coef-infinity-normalized-final-cone] supplies a normalized initial join cone. Precompose its simplexwise cone maps with $\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to\Delta^0\star\Delta^n$, sending $(a,0)$ to the initial vertex and $(a,1)$ to $a$; these agree on faces and degeneracies. This gives $\alpha:S_r\times\Delta^1\to S_r$ from the constant functor at $1_r$ to $\mathrm{id}_{S_r}$, constant on $\{1_r\}\times\Delta^1$. The projection $\pi:D_r\to S_r$ is a pullback of the right fibration $q$; its fibre over $1_r$ is strictly $E_r$, with inclusion $i$. Prescribe $\mathrm{id}$ on $D_r\times\{1\}$ and $i\operatorname{pr}$ on $E_r\times\Delta^1$ over $\alpha(\pi\times\mathrm{id})$; this commutes since $\alpha(-,1)=\mathrm{id}$ and $\alpha$ is constant on $\{1_r\}\times\Delta^1$. Passing to opposites ($\{1\}$ becomes $\{0\}$, $\pi^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a left fibration), [lem-coef-left-fibration-relative-cylinder-lifting] with $K=D_r^{\mathrm{op}}$, $A=E_r^{\mathrm{op}}$ gives $\widetilde\alpha:D_r\times\Delta^1\to D_r$ over $\alpha(\pi\times\mathrm{id})$ extending these data. Its restriction $T$ to $D_r\times\{0\}$ lies over $1_r$, so lands in $E_r$, and $Ti=\mathrm{id}$. Thus $\widetilde\alpha$ and the projection homotopy make $i$ a weak homotopy equivalence by [lem-cbc-simplicial-homotopy-equivalence-weak]. By step 5, $E_r$ is weakly contractible; it is Kan by [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-fibers]. Now [lem-coef-right-fibration-contractible-fibers] applies for every $r$, and makes $q$ a trivial Kan fibration.

source.place: Agent deformation of the right-fibration comma onto its fibre, using the initial identity arrow; no classification or space-valued straightening theorem.

proof.text: A trivial Kan fibration lifts every monomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-lifts-monomorphisms]. Cofibrations in the Joyal model structure are exactly monomorphisms, and their right lifting class is the trivial fibrations, by [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Thus $q$ is a Joyal weak equivalence. Apply [lem-coef-joyal-functor-equivalence-test] to the actual map $q$: precomposition $q^*:\operatorname{Fun}(R,D)\to\operatorname{Fun}(E,D)$ is a functor equivalence. Its map on every mapping space is an equivalence by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], hence restriction along $q$ is an equivalence on the required cocone spaces. Restriction along $j$ is an equivalence by [lem-coef-infinity-anodyne-cocones]. Their composite is restriction itself along $qj=k$, with the asserted naturality and postcomposition compatibility.

source.place: Agent conclusion from right-anodyne factorization; compare the cocone restriction formulation of Theorem 6.4.5. The proof does not cite the downstream comma-cofinality criterion.

proof.text: For a specified cocone $\lambda:V\to\Delta d$, use the colimit criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus]: for every $x$, the map $\operatorname{Map}_D(d,x)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(R,D)}(V,\Delta x)$ must be an equivalence. Step 7 identifies this test with that for $\lambda k$. Both implications follow. If a colimit is initially specified only on $Vk$, essential surjectivity of the cocone-space equivalence with fixed apex $d$ lifts it to a cocone on $V$, up to equivalence; the same test proves this lift colimiting. All horn factorization and deformation took place in a universe containing the whole $R$. For any further $D$, enlarge again to contain $D$ and these simplicial sets; the comparisons remain the actual restriction maps, so the argument has exactly the universe scope in the statement.
